subsystems.name: Reasoning and planning core
subsystems.role: proposes hypotheses and designs experiments to test them.
parts: large language model or hybrid AI

subsystems.name: Robotic execution platform
subsystems.role: physically carries out the experiments the planner requests.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline and analysis
subsystems.role: captures results, analyses them, and feeds them back to the planner.

subsystems.name: Knowledge integration
subsystems.role: grounds the agent in existing literature and prior results.

subsystems.name: Safety and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps experiments safe and results trustworthy.

buildSteps.title: Choose a domain
buildSteps.detail: Pick a narrow scientific field such as materials synthesis or drug formulation, and define the vocabulary of actions and measurements the agent will use.

buildSteps.title: Curate training data
buildSteps.detail: Collect papers, lab protocols, and experimental datasets so the model can learn what a good hypothesis and a valid experiment look like.

buildSteps.title: Train or fine-tune the model
buildSteps.detail: Adapt a large language model to propose hypotheses, rank them, and translate them into step-by-step experimental plans.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with lab robots
buildSteps.detail: Write software adapters so the planner can command liquid handlers, robotic arms, and instruments through their APIs or a standard lab-automation language.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect planning, execution, and analysis so results automatically update the agent's beliefs and trigger the next experiment.

buildSteps.title: Validate against known results
buildSteps.detail: Have the agent reproduce experiments with known outcomes, and compare its proposed plans with those of human experts.

buildSteps.title: Add safety checks
buildSteps.detail: Encode physical and chemical safety limits, and keep a human able to pause or override the system.

buildSteps.title: Deploy on a real problem
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent on a specific discovery task, with human scientists reviewing results, then gradually widen its scope.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with scientific reasoning
prerequisites.why: they provide the hypothesis-generation and planning capability, though deep scientific reasoning is still limited.
many instruments can be automated, but few labs are fully robot-ready and hardware is often bespoke.
proprietary APIs and data formats make it hard for one agent to control many different instruments.
methods such as Bayesian optimisation already choose experiments efficiently in narrow settings.
much experimental data is unpublished or in inconsistent formats, limiting what agents can learn from.
there is no established way to certify that an autonomous agent will not run dangerous or invalid experiments.

pathway.milestone: demonstrations such as A-Lab and Coscientist show closed-loop discovery in narrow domains
pathway.unlocks: proof that an AI agent can design, run, and interpret experiments without step-by-step human control.

pathway.milestone: cloud labs expose standard APIs so agents can run experiments remotely across many instruments
pathway.unlocks: scalable, around-the-clock experimentation without building a new lab for every project.

pathway.milestone: agents that formulate novel hypotheses and design multi-step experiments, with human oversight
pathway.unlocks: faster discovery in materials science, drug discovery, and chemistry.

pathway.milestone: self-improving agents that operate across several scientific domains
pathway.unlocks: continuous, automated scientific progress — if safety, verification, and data-sharing problems are solved.
